insight.title: The Manager Who Told His Engineer to Take Off His Hat
insight.subtitle: How a single sentence silenced the engineers warning of the Challenger disaster.

sections.text: January 27, 1986. Engineers fought desperately to halt the Challenger launch. Freezing temperatures would ruin the rocket's rubber seals. But NASA was furious about delays, demanding an immediate, final decision.
Pressured, executive Jerry Mason turned to his hesitating vice president of engineering. He uttered the fatal command: "Take off your engineering hat and put on your management hat."
The engineer yielded and signed the launch approval. The next morning, seventy-three seconds after liftoff, the frozen seals failed, destroying the shuttle and killing all seven crew members.
Physics does not care about management hats.
